correctness.rationale: For a word of length n the visited Cayley vertices form a finite Munn subtree T. Inverse-semigroup identities characterize R by T, L by endpoint-translated T, and D by translation classes of the unrooted labelled T. Any walk visiting all tree edges from s to t has minimum 2(|V(T)|-1)-d(s,t), attained by doubled excursions from the s-t path. Optimizing free roots yields precisely the three stated distances. There are <=n+1 prefix vertices. Repeated reductions and equality/distance scans use O(n) work cells and halt in polynomial time. Replayed finite verifier exhaustively checked 9,063 words in ranks 1,2,3 by class-minimum enumeration. This is supporting finite evidence, not the general proof.

value.rationale: The new complexity bound resolves the context-sensitivity part of a specific published open question for all three Green relations at every finite rank, simultaneously classifying the languages and their complements inside context-sensitive languages. Its reusable-storage tree-geometry algorithm avoids an unrestricted search over shorter words. The result has a direct algorithmic and formal-language-theoretic use independent of any arbitrary finite parameter and does not assert a resolution of the remaining indexed-language question.
